sources.title: Datum Atlas compilation of end-of-life data: recycling energy and CO₂, recycled fractions, heats of combustion and combustion CO₂
sources.author: Datum Atlas contributors
sources.note: Typical ranges by material class. Recycling energy and CO₂ are a share of the primary values (scrap-based metal, cullet, regranulate); recycled fractions follow the recycling shares in public statistics; heats of combustion and combustion CO₂ follow from the chemical composition (carbon content). Draft.

sources.title: Life Cycle Assessment of Metals: A Scientific Synthesis (PLOS ONE 9(7): e101298)
sources.author: P. Nuss and M.J. Eckelman
sources.note: Cradle-to-gate cumulative energy demand and greenhouse-gas emissions of 63 metals, per kg of element, with 2.5 to 97.5 % ranges (Supporting Information S1, Table S38). Embodied energy and CO₂ of each metal here: the element's own production route for Al, Mg, Ti, Zn, Sn, Co, V, Be and Zr, pig iron for Fe, and the overall figure of the element for Cu, Ni, Pb, W, Cr, Mn and Mo; alloys combine their elements by nominal mass fraction (primary metal content only: making the alloy, refining and shaping are not included).

sources.title: Datum Atlas compilation of the properties of the elements
sources.author: Datum Atlas contributors
sources.licence: MIT (this compilation); written from public-domain US government data
sources.note: Category, state, density, melting and boiling points, crystal structure, electronegativity and lattice parameters of the 118 elements, compiled by us from the PubChem periodic table (US National Library of Medicine, public domain) and general crystallography texts. Draft: values are to be checked one by one; gaps where no reliable value is known.

sources.title: Standard atomic weights

sources.note: Conventional atomic weights, rounded to five significant figures or fewer; for elements without a standard weight, the mass number of the longest-lived isotope.

sources.title: Electrical energy requirements for manufacturing processes
sources.author: T. Gutowski, J. Dahmus and A. Thiriez (MIT)

sources.title: Datum Atlas compilation of manufacturing processes and processing ratings
sources.author: Datum Atlas contributors
sources.note: Typical capabilities of each process (part mass, section, shapes, tolerance, roughness, economic batch) and indicative costs (tooling, rate, overhead, scrap), and castability, machinability and weldability by material class, written from general engineering knowledge. Draft: indicative ranges, not quotes; ask your supplier.
